title: Overlapping Work

story.briefing: The access shaft has n rungs. A climber takes one or two at a time. Before the Core will open it wants to know exactly how many distinct climbs exist.
story.success: Climb count accepted. The shaft unseals.

description: A climber ascends n rungs, moving either one or two rungs at each step. Return how many distinct sequences of steps reach the top exactly. There is exactly one way to climb 0 rungs: take no steps.

examples.explanation: Taking no steps is one way.

hints: The last step onto rung n came from either rung n-1 or rung n-2. So the count for n is the sum of the counts for those two.
Written as plain recursion this recomputes the same rungs enormous numbers of times — the call count itself grows exponentially. Each rung answer only needs computing once.
Work upward instead of downward. Start with the answers for 0 and 1 rungs, then compute each rung from the two below it. Only the last two values are ever needed, so two variables suffice.
